A1.justification: Both ten-page PDFs describe the same DEUS work, with readable and directly matchable text, equations, tables and figures. Neither includes the Appendices A and D referenced in the text; this comparison covers the supplied documents, not unavailable supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original DEUS evaluations on three OWOD benchmarks, component ablations, feature analyses and qualitative detection results in Tables 1–3 and Figures 1, 3 and 4.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original benchmark evaluations, ablations and analyses. Retained results still qualify as original empirical results.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.4 retain the same OrthogonalDet-based architecture, EUS and EKD losses, and inference calibration. Figure 2 corrects subspace labels without changing the described procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate M-OWODB, S-OWODB and DIOR-based RS-OWODB, retaining the same natural-image and remote-sensing coverage and incremental detection tasks.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains ORE, OW-DETR, CAT, PROB, OrthogonalDet, O1O and OWOBJ. Table 2 retains OrthogonalDet as the RS-OWODB comparator; no comparator membership changes.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the four-task evaluation, mAP, unknown recall and H-Score metrics, and stated experimental settings. Table 1 also retains the same annotation-duplication correction note.

E4.justification: The EUS/EKD ablations in Table 3, proposal and energy-score analyses in Figures 1 and 3, and qualitative case study in Figure 4 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or experimental error bars. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–3 and the empirical figures are unchanged. For example, DEUS retains M-OWODB unknown recalls of 65.1, 66.2 and 69.0 for Tasks 1–3; the reported computational overheads also remain identical.

T1.justification: The problem definition and Equations 1–17 are unchanged. Correcting the reversed subspace symbols in Figure 2 aligns the illustration with existing definitions rather than revising mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning unknown-object representation learning, reduced interference during replay, and benchmark performance.

C2.justification: The interpretations of EUS separation, EKD interference reduction and remote-sensing generalization remain identical. The conclusion retains the same limitation concerning semantic overlap between known and unknown objects.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 retains MMDetection, K=128, 64 vectors per subspace, unit loss weights, and the same replay and pseudo-labeling disclosures. Both versions refer to absent appendices for further details; neither adds implementation or resource-access information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, positioning against prior energy-based approaches, and all 26 references are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 31 March 2026 to v2 dated 28 May 2026. The prose, section organization, title and author information remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is slightly redrawn and corrects reversed labels: v1 labels the unknown space W^E_K and known space W^E_U, while v2 correctly uses W^E_U and W^E_K, respectively. Other figures, tables and the surrounding page layout remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Correcting Figure 2 removes a misleading reversal in the central method illustration and makes it consistent with Equations 5–6. This provides a limited improvement in clarity and internal consistency; the scientific content, evidence and reproducibility disclosures otherwise remain unchanged.
